# Downstream SolidCore changes

`face37.patch` changes the implementation of planar Face 37 (hole-loop nesting) in the pinned SolidCore revision. The public kernel check level and tolerances are unchanged. The patch and the original/patched file hashes are in [the lock file](../solidcore.lock.json). The local vendor tool and native Linux image both verify the patch before compiling it.

For a planar face with at least four loops, the check builds each inner loop's UV control-polygon bounds at most once. A B-spline on its natural knot interval with positive finite rational weights lies inside its Euclidean control hull. The winding of such a loop cannot put a point strictly outside the expanded hull inside the loop. Only the inner-versus-inner **Inside** predicate uses this exclusion. The outer-loop classification is unchanged. Unknown or missing trims, an edge interval extending beyond the curve's domain, nonpositive or nonfinite weights, non-planar faces, and points near or inside the expanded bounds all use the upstream classifier. Every loop still participates in Level‑1.

This replaces expensive distant pair classifications with cheap comparisons; it does **not** make the pair enumeration subquadratic. Independent checks on the face, surface, edge, vertex and topology still run, including the manifold and mass-property checks in Colocad. See [the native negative regression](../../crates/agent-cad/tests/level1_nesting.rs).

`validation-properties.patch` accelerates the minimum-speed and minimum-curvature-radius tests on spline trims. It is enabled when Colocad inspects terminal bodies in plain assemblies. A clamped rational quadratic curve qualifies only if each knot span is a quadratic Bézier span, its positive weights and coordinate range satisfy the numerical guards, and a conservative lower bound exceeds the native threshold by a factor of eight. The code bounds the derivative using its Bernstein poles. It bounds curvature radius using speed squared divided by an upper bound on acceleration. The checks use one-sided bounds at knots. Existing knot, continuity, topology and manifold checks still execute. Mapped trim curvature uses its original solver. Ambiguous spans and the stricter solver-status policy also retain the generic path.

The same patch can reuse a completed pure spline solve for bit-identical poles, knots, curve flags, interval, property and separation. Changes to kernel settings invalidate the cache. The cache stores successful results with at most 16 solution ends and caps key and value payload at 1 MiB and 512 entries per kernel. Cancellable operations bypass both shortcuts. [Comparison against native failure reports](../../crates/agent-cad/tests/validation_properties.rs)

`planar-conic-domain.patch` supplements sampled planar STEP parameter boxes with the stationary points of each bounded Circle/Ellipse projected onto the plane's U/V axes. A projection is `A cos(t) + B sin(t)`; its derivative zeros recur every 180 degrees. The mapper restricts conic edge spans to at most one turn, so at most three stationary candidates per axis cover either edge sense, including a wrapped interval. A constant projection adds no candidates. Existing samples and bounds remain; no curve, topology, tolerance, assertion or error policy is changed. Non-planar surfaces, Lines and B-splines retain their previous path; this is **not** a general B-spline bound fix.

The patch addresses an underestimated sampled domain that can send a planar rational-curve drop through clamping/fallback and lose an arc segment. Synthetic continuous-extrema, reversed interval, tilted plane, wrap, full turn and degenerate-projection cases are in `step_planar_conic_domain.rs`. A corrupted UV trim must still trigger the existing loop-gap check. The G3-B long-arc source is a private cross-check only: same mechanism and coverage remain unconfirmed until a fresh first-check Windows receipt. All runtime validation for this candidate is Windows/WSL2-only and currently pending.

The closed-solid delivery control in `step_planar_conic_delivery.rs` rotates the seam of the public drilled-block fixture by 17 degrees together with both circular edges, cylindrical reference frame, corresponding plane pcurves, vertices and seam line. It exercises native import/build/export/readback and a deliberately inconsistent seam-vertex negative. This is a full-delivery non-regression control; it is not required to fail before the patch because the outer rectangular face already bounds the bore. Independent Windows OCP material comparisons remain unknown until actual receipts. No generated fixture, local geometry execution or G1 workaround is part of this candidate.

The spline validation overlay also reports raw and tolerance-grouped endpoint knot multiplicities, along with curve dimension and degree, when the current endpoint check fails. The predicate is unchanged.
